x: It was encouraging to see Gerry Cameron finish so well in this his first try-out over 10 miles and also to have Bernard Eglinton back home again after three years abroad and pushing the lads once more.
Ken Bailey seemed to be doing a steady training spin, while the extra miles suited Bernard Eglinton who shows steady improvement on each outing since his return from abroad.

Morris followed our eighth man in closely, and with Bernard Eglinton and Harry Shields completed our 'B' team. Meanwhile Ken Mathews had recorded an easy win having led from start to finish in his first 20 miles Championship, pursued by Don Thompson the holder.
Ray forged on to win with Pat "I left it at Leicester" being pipped for second place. Dave King and Bernard Eglinton both fresh from the Mercury walked magnificently to bring the team in 2nd equal.

Both John Keown and Bernard Eglinton have backed up our recognised distance men but youth is not on their side and I am sure that they would be as pleased as the rest of us to be forced out by a rising tide of enthusiasm from below.

Further back Keown was moving along well, ahead of Bob Picton and Bernard Eglinton. Our two soigneurs Ray Hall and Harry Shields performed noble feats of endurance with the sponge and bottle and by the start of the third lap Belgrave looked well placed although Bob was forced to retire.
Dave King started steadily, mindful of his retirement last year, with Johnny Morris John Keown and Bernard Eglinton packing well a little further back.
Thorpe fell back some forty minutes with Guy Goodair also of Wakefield coming through to second place some 12 minutes behind the leader. Once again Bernard Eglinton beat 10 hours to finish 31st.
Bernard Eglinton also turned in a useful performance so that had the captain been a prophet we could also have taken the Milan Trophy for the first team to finish eight.

George Beecham moved through steadily to back up our faster men but the real performance of the day came from Bernard Eglinton who not only held George to two minutes but came within an ace of taking the first veterans prize as well.
Insurance policy Bernard Eglinton was not up to his usual form and for him the road was long. At Croydon the leading group began to break up Eley taking the lead with Fogg dropping back.
It was great to see Bernard Eglinton back in the bunch again, his 56:30 gave him a pleasant suprise and showed that it can't all be lost in Wales.

In one of his cheery letters from Colwyn Bay, Bernard Eglinton recalls that when stationed with the R.A.F. in Germany in 1954/57 he walked in Amsterdam, Eindhoven and Rotterdam over 20 and 50 Kilos.

Bernard Eglinton has been training hard on the front at Colwyn Bay with the object of the Marathon. At 68 years of age he has an impressive list of runs and long-distance walks to his name and he achieved his objective in a race from Queensferry to Prestatyn in which he finished in 4.45.06.

My main recollection of this rave was the comment from Bernard Eglinton who having travelled all the way from Colwyn Bay and been delayed by the trains, walked into the hall to ask "what job can I do?".
BERNARD EGLINTON - Ex R.A.F. regular who joined the club as a runner from Derby AC and eventually excelled as a walker and scored in a number of National 50kms and 20mls R.W.A.
